titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spell 17, part 6
part: Spell 17, part 6 — the phallus of Osiris, the hair of Isis, and Wadjet (Plate 10)
about: The last part of Spell 17 on Ani's papyrus is a run of statements, each followed by the gloss that explains it. A being called Rehu, bright of mouth, is told to turn back, and is explained as the phallus of Osiris, or of Ra; Isis loosens(?) her hair over her brow and hides in it; and Wadjet, lady of flame(?), is the Eye of Ra. Many words here are rare and some readings are doubtful. On the papyrus it runs over Plate 10, lines 133 to 145, where the chapter ends.

sentences.l: behind-you · Rehu · bright · of-mouth · moving(?) · of-head · retreat · because-of · might-his
sentences.i: Back, Rehu, bright of mouth, moving(?) of head! Retreat before his might!
sentences.n: The first sign of ḥꜣ·k is printed before Budge's numeral 133, so the word strictly begins at the end of line 132; the unit is placed at line 133, where the rest of it stands. ḥꜣ·k is the papyrus clump ḥꜣ (M16) with ꜣ as its complement and a small head (D1; perhaps the back of the head) as classifier, and ·k: the preposition ḥꜣ 'behind' with a suffix, 'behind you!', the cry that sends something back. rḥw is the lion rw, standing here for r, with a stroke, the wick ḥ, w and a seated god: Rehu, a being not otherwise named in these parts (Budge: Reḥu); the published parts have rḥwy 'the Two Companions', and this may be its singular. ḥḏ rꜣ 'bright of mouth' is the mace ḥḏ (T3, joined with the cobra ḏ) with the sun, and the mouth with its stroke; psd tp is p, the bolt s and the hand d, with a leg as classifier, and the head: taken as 'moving(?) of head', a verb of movement by its classifier; the word is not known otherwise (Budge: peṭes, with d before s; the type sets p over s and the hand after them, and the gloss in line 143, where Budge reads pest, has the same signs, so the reading follows the signs), and the gloss in line 143 repeats it. Both are adjective-and-noun phrases describing Rehu. ḥm 'retreat' is the well ḥm (coded N41, approximate) with m and walking legs, an imperative; n is 'because of'; pḥty·f 'his might' is the rump pḥ, t, two strokes y and a leopard's head (F9), the usual classifier of the word, with ·f. Whose might is meant is not said. The gloss in line 143 says what Rehu is.

sentences.l: another · saying · drives-back · him · the-one-who-does · guarding · not · can-be-seen-he · the-guardian(?)
sentences.i: Another saying: the one who keeps watch drives him back; he cannot be seen, the guardian(?).
sentences.n: The papyrus writes all of this in red: a variant of 'retreat before his might', brought in by ky ḏd 'another saying' as in part 5. ḥm is written as in the line before, with the rump (F22) added to the walking legs as a second classifier of going back. A dependent pronoun object stands before a noun subject, so ḥm sw iri sꜣw is read 'the one who keeps watch drives him back', with ḥm used transitively; read as an imperative, 'turn back from him who keeps watch' (Budge's sense), it would need a preposition that is not written. It could also be an imperative with its object and a vocative, 'drive him back, you who keep watch'. iri is the eye ir with r, the participle of iri 'do, make'; sꜣw 'guarding' is the seated herdsman with his stick (A47), the sign that writes sꜣw 'guard, keep watch', with ꜣ and w as complements and a low sign coded U15: iri sꜣw 'who keeps watch'. Budge's numeral 134 is printed inside sꜣw. n mꜣꜣ·n·tw·f is the negative n (D35, the arms held out, with water n; the type shows a stroke with a raised step) before the sḏm·n·f made passive with tw: 'he cannot be seen'. mꜣꜣ is the eye joined with the sickle mꜣ (U1) and ꜣ; then n, tw (t and w) and ·f. sꜣwty, the herdsman again with ꜣ, w, t and two strokes y (the bird coded G43, approximate, holds a stick), is taken as the nisba 'the guardian', in apposition to 'he' (Budge reads it with the next words, 'guarded is the Osiris Ani'). The sense of the variant is doubtful.

sentences.i: The Osiris Ani: he is Isis.
sentences.n: The text is black again. wsir is the low seat with the eye, as in part 5; ꜣny as always. ntf 'he' is the independent pronoun, n, t and f, as in ntf tm 'he is Atum' at the end of part 5: ntf N 'he is N', a sentence without a verb, with the Osiris Ani put first as its topic. ꜣst 'Isis' is the seat with t and the egg (H8), written as in part 5; Budge's transliteration under it is printed 'Àusct', a misprint of his for Àuset. That the dead man takes the name of a goddess is no difficulty in this book; what follows, the loosened hair, is the gesture of Isis mourning Osiris.

sentences.l: has-found-he · him · loosens(?)-he · the-hair · of · face-his · tangle(?)-I · at · brow-his
sentences.i: He has found him, as he loosens(?) the hair of his face; I tangle(?) it at his brow.
sentences.n: gm·n·f is the ibis gm (G28) with m, then t and the roll, and n and ·f: the sḏm·n·f of gmi 'find', 'he has found'; the t and the roll are written as in the infinitive gmt and are not read. Budge's numeral 135 is printed inside the word. sw 'him'. psḫ·f is p, the bolt s, the placenta ḫ and walking legs, and ·f; the p and the s are Budge's restoration of damage, inside his square brackets. It is the sḏm·f after the object of 'find', 'as he loosens(?)'; the gloss in line 144 writes the word with d, psdḫ, and the verb is not known otherwise: 'loosen, spread out (the hair)' is the sense the gloss and Budge's 'spreadeth' point to, and it is doubtful. šny is the cord šn (V7) with n, the lock of hair (D3) and two strokes: šn 'hair'. n ḥr·f 'of his face' is the genitive n and the face with ·f. tḫtḫ·i is t and ḫ written twice, the lock of hair and the seated man ·i: a reduplicated verb of the hair, taken as 'tangle, put in disorder' (Budge: teχteχ, 'scatter'); doubtful. r is written with a stroke, as often on this papyrus. wpt·f 'his brow' is the horns wp (F13) with t and a stroke (Budge reads àpt): the brow or the top of the head. The pronouns are not clear: 'he' may be Ani as Isis, 'him' Osiris. The gloss in line 144 explains these words as Isis hiding in her hair.

sentences.l: was-conceived-he · in · Isis · was-begotten-he · in · Nephthys
sentences.i: He was conceived in Isis and begotten in Nephthys.
sentences.n: iwr·n·f is the recumbent calf iw (E9) with w, the swallow wr with r, and the pregnant woman (B2) as classifier, then n and ·f: the sḏm·n·f of iwr 'conceive', used of the child, 'he was conceived', as iwr·i 'I was conceived' in Spell 1. bnn·n·f is the foot b and water n twice, with the phallus (D53) as classifier, and n and ·f: the sḏm·n·f of bnn 'beget', in the same use, 'he was begotten' (Budge: bennen). m 'in' is the owl; after verbs of conceiving it names the mother. ꜣst has the snake (I12) after the egg; nbt-ḥwt 'Nephthys' is the enclosure with the basket and a snake, as in part 5. Who 'he' is, the text does not say; the two sisters share the birth, as they share the mourning of Osiris.

sentences.i: They hack down his strife(?).
sentences.n: bḥn·sn is the foot b, the wick ḥ and water n, with a second n as complement, a knife (T30) and the low sign coded U15 as classifiers, and ·sn 'they' (the bolt s, n and plural strokes): the sḏm·f of bḥn 'cut, hack', 'they hack' (Budge: beḥenen-sen). 'They' are Isis and Nephthys of the line before. ḫnnw·f is ḫ (the first sign is coded Aa1 only as a placeholder: the type shows a slanting stick with a loop crossing a frame, a sign not identified), n, n with the pot nw and w, the low sign again and plural strokes, and ·f: taken as ḫnnw 'strife, disturbance', as in the Spell 125 declarations, here 'his strife', what troubles him; Budge took it for 'the things which should be cut away from him'. Because the first sign is not identified, the reading is doubtful.

sentences.i: Fear is behind you, and dread of you is upon his arms.
sentences.n: nrw is r printed over water n, then w, a small curled sign (coded V1, approximate; not identified) and a stroke: read nrw 'fear, terror', with Budge, the n read first though the r stands above it; the curl may be the classifier. m-ḫt·k 'behind you' is the owl m and the sign ḫt (M3) with ḫ and t as complements and walking legs, and ·k: the compound preposition m-ḫt 'after, behind'. nrw m-ḫt·k is a sentence without a verb, noun and prepositional phrase. šfšft·k is š and f twice, t, and a small ram (coded E10, approximate) with a stroke, and ·k: šfšft 'dread, awe', with the ram, its usual classifier; 'your dread' is the dread you inspire. tp 'upon' is the head with its stroke. ꜥwy·f 'his two arms' is the arm with a stroke, the arm again for the dual, w and two strokes y, and ·f. 'You' is the god addressed; 'he' is not named.

sentences.i: Your arm is against millions, against their shoulders(?); you have gone round the common folk(?).
sentences.n: qꜥḥ·k is the hill q, the arm ꜥ and the wick ḥ, with the bent arm (D41) as classifier, a stroke and a small curl (coded Z7, approximate; it may be the piece of flesh F51), and ·k: qꜥḥ 'shoulder, arm', as in Spell 1. r 'against'. ḥḥ 'millions' is the kneeling god Heh (C11) with a stroke and plural strokes. rmn·sn is r and the gaming board mn (Y5) with n, the bent arm, the curl and strokes, and ·sn: rmn 'shoulder, upper arm', 'their shoulders' (a dashed stroke stands between the word and ·sn). rr·n·k is an elongated loop open at one end (coded V10, approximate; perhaps a long r) and r, with walking legs, and n and ·k: taken as the sḏm·n·f of a verb rr 'go round, encircle', with Budge's 'go round', 'you have gone round'; it could also be rr n·k rḫyt 'the common folk go round for you'. rḫyt 'the common folk' is the lapwing (G24) with t and plural strokes. The construction of the first clause is not clear: the shoulders are taken as standing beside 'millions'. Budge's 'embraced art thou for millions of years by their arms' reads qꜥḥ as a verb in the passive, with a preposition that is not written. Both clauses are doubtful.

sentences.i: You strike down(?) the wentu(?) of your enemy; you have lifted the confederates(?) by their shoulders.
sentences.n: sbḫbḫ·k is the folded cloth s, then b and ḫ, b and ḫ, a second ḫ, t, walking legs and ·k. The signs give s-b-ḫ-b-ḫ; Budge reads seχebχeb, 'thou smitest down', with ḫ before b in the first pair. Neither form is known otherwise, the t is not accounted for, and the sense 'strike down' is Budge's and doubtful; it is read as the signs stand, a sḏm·f, 'you strike down(?)'. wntw is the flower wn (coded M42, approximate; the type shows a four-petalled flower over a basin), t and w, with two seated figures and a stroke, the classifier of people: a class of beings, not known otherwise (Budge: untu, 'advocates'), followed directly by ḫfty·k, 'your enemy', ḫ, f and t with the kneeling enemy (coded A14, approximate) and a stroke (the y is not written); the two nouns side by side make the genitive. fꜣ·n·k is f and ꜣ, with a loop-on-base sign (coded F22, approximate) and the roll, and n and ·k: the sḏm·n·f of fꜣi 'lift, carry', 'you have lifted'. smꜣyw is the bolt s, a hatched oblong with a cross (coded N37, approximate), m, two reeds and a seated figure with a stroke. Budge reads Sami; that reading needs the oblong to be the lung and windpipe smꜣ (F36), and it is taken so here, as smꜣyw 'the confederates', the gang of Seth; read as š, the group would spell sšmyw, perhaps 'leaders' (from sšm 'lead'), which suits a sentence about enemies less well; either way the reading is doubtful. rmn·sn 'their shoulders' has two bent arms, the dual; 'by' is not written. The whole is doubtful.

sentences.i: The two sisters are given to you as your delight.
sentences.n: Budge's group erṭā-nek is split here into rdi and n·k. rdi is r and the giving arm di: the passive sḏm of rdi 'give', 'are given', as in part 5, with n·k 'to you', water n and ·k. snty is the arrowhead sn (T22) twice, each with water n: the dual written by repeating the word, read snty 'the two sisters' (the t of the feminine is not written; the group could also be snwy 'the two brothers'). Budge reads 'the two sisters', and Isis and Nephthys have just been named. bnri·k is the foot b, n, r and a reed, with the sign of bnr 'sweet' (M30, approximate) and the roll as classifiers, and ·k: bnri 'sweetness, delight'; 'as' is supplied.

sentences.i: You create the one who is in Kher-aba(?), the one who is in Heliopolis.
sentences.n: qmꜣ·k is the hill q, the sickle mꜣ (U1) with ꜣ and m as complements, a plant (coded M2, approximate; the type shows a stalk joined with a bird pecking down), the roll and a stroke, and ·k: qmꜣ 'create', a sḏm·f, 'you create'. Budge's numeral 139 is printed inside it. imy is the sign im (Z11) with m and two strokes y: the nisba of m 'in', 'the one who is in', twice. The place is the sign ẖr (T28) with r, a stela (O26) with a low mound (coded N29, approximate) at its foot, ꜣ, the low sign coded U15 and the town sign. Budge reads Kher-āba; the stela is given the value ꜥbꜣ that his reading needs, which is not a usual value of it. The name may well be the town Kher-aha (ḫr-ꜥḥꜣ) by Heliopolis, which the Spell 125 declarations name next to Heliopolis; but the signs do not spell ꜥḥꜣ, and a stela in place of the group ꜥḥꜣ is not a dropped or doubled sign or a wrong classifier, so the misprints rule does not apply: the name is given as the signs stand, ẖr-ꜥbꜣ, and the reading is doubtful. iwnw 'Heliopolis' is the pillar iwn with the pot nw and the town sign.

sentences.l: god · every · fears · [n] · of-you · great · very · dread-your
sentences.i: Every god is afraid of you; very great is your dread.
sentences.n: nṯr nb 'every god' is the flag with a seated god, and the basket nb, 'every' after its noun. snḏ 'fear' is the plucked goose snḏ (G54, approximate) with the man with hand to mouth (A2): a sḏm·f after its noun subject, 'every god fears'. snḏ n 'be afraid of' takes the preposition n; here water n is written twice, n n·k. The first n is taken as a doubled sign and not translated; it could be the n of a sḏm·n·f, but then the god would stand after the verb. wrt is the swallow wr with r and t: wr 'great'. In a sentence of quality the adjective in front normally takes no ending, so the t is unexpected: it may be written by attraction to the feminine šfšft, or wrt may be the adverb 'greatly'; ꜥꜣ 'very' is the column ꜥꜣ (O29) with the arm ꜥ and the roll, an adverb after an adjective. wrt ꜥꜣ šfšft·k is a sentence of quality, the adjective first: 'very great is your dread'. šfšft·k as in line 136, without the stroke.

sentences.i: Every god is in the hand of(?) the one who curses him, shooting(?) […].
sentences.n: The sentence is not clear. nṯr nb 'every god' again; Budge prints a footnote after nṯr here, thinking a word was lost. m-ꜥ is the owl m and the arm ꜥ joined in one group: the compound preposition 'in the hand of, with; from (the hand of)'. As the words stand, nṯr nb m-ꜥ … is a complete sentence without a verb, a noun with a prepositional phrase as its predicate, 'every god is in the hand of …', and it is taken so here; if a verb has been lost, as Budge thought, m-ꜥ would rather be 'from (the hand of)'. sḥwri is the folded cloth s, the wick ḥ, the swallow wr with r, a reed and the man with hand to mouth (A2): the participle of sḥwr 'curse', 'the one who curses', with sw 'him' as its object. stt is the pierced skin st (F29) with t twice: taken as the infinitive of sti 'shoot' (Budge: satet, 'shooting arrows'), but this is a guess. After it the papyrus has a group of three signs, the arrowhead sn (T22), a stroke and the house sign (the type shows a rectangle open below), under which Budge prints no transliteration and only dots in his English. It is given here as sn by its first sign and left untranslated: what it is, is not clear.

morph.gloss: unclear: a group of the arrowhead sn, a stroke and the house sign, which Budge leaves untransliterated

sentences.l: live-you · according-to · wish-your · you · Wadjet · lady · of-flame(?)
sentences.i: You live as you wish; you are Wadjet, lady of flame(?).
sentences.n: ꜥnḫ·k is the sign ꜥnḫ (S34) with n and ḫ as complements, and ·k: a sḏm·f, 'you live'. r here is 'according to'. mry·k is the hoe mr (U6) with r, two reeds y and the man with hand to mouth, and ·k: mri 'wish, desire' used as a noun after r, 'your wish' (the infinitive would be mrt, with a t that is not written here). ntk 'you' is the independent pronoun, n, t and k: ntk N 'you are N', a sentence without a verb. wꜣḏyt is the papyrus stem wꜣḏ (M13) with the cobra ḏ twined round it in one group, two reeds y, t and a snake (I12): Wadjet, the cobra goddess of Lower Egypt (Budge: Uatchit). nbt 'lady' is the basket nb with t. imw is a reed, the sign im (Z11) with m, w, and the flame (Q7, approximate; the type shows a tall loop knotted at the foot) with a stroke: a word for flame or burning, not known otherwise, read with the flame as its classifier (Budge: àmmu, 'flame'); doubtful. The gloss in line 145 explains Wadjet as the Eye of Ra.

sentences.i: They come up to you, and few are there among them(?).
sentences.n: Budge's group āri-sen-nek is split here into ꜥry·sn and n·k. ꜥry·sn is the arm ꜥ, r and two strokes y, with a beam on a stand with two loops above it (coded U38, approximate; not identified) as classifier, and ·sn: taken as ꜥri 'go up, approach', a sḏm·f, 'they come up', with n·k 'to you' (Budge: 'those who rise up against thee'). ꜥnd is the arm ꜥ, n and the hand d, with the small bird of bad things (G37) and plural strokes: ꜥnd 'few, little, lacking', the sparrow being the classifier of what is small. im·sn is a reed and the owl m, the form of the preposition m before a suffix, 'among them'. ꜥnd im·sn is read 'few (are there) among them', that is, they dwindle; Budge's 'evil [cometh] among them' takes the bird for the sense. The sentence is doubtful.

sentences.i: What, then, is it?
sentences.n: The question, in red, written as in part 5, here all of it red. The answer, in black, gives names; it does not say which words of the statement it explains.

sentences.l: secret · of-forms · whom-gives · Menhu · the-name · of · the-shrine(?)
sentences.i: 'Secret of forms, whom Menhu gives' is the name of the shrine(?).
sentences.n: štꜣ 'secret' is the pool š, t and the kiln tꜣ (coded U30, approximate) with ꜣ, the crossed sticks (Z9) and the roll; irw 'forms' is a reed, the eye ir and w, with a mummiform figure (A53), the roll and a stroke: štꜣ irw, adjective and noun, 'secret of forms'. dd is the giving arm twice, the form of rdi 'give' with doubled d used for the imperfective: taken as the relative form, 'whom (Menhu) gives', with mnḥw its subject (Budge: 'given by'). mnḥw is the gaming board mn with n, the wick ḥ and w, and a seated god: Menhu, a god (Budge: Menḥu). Budge's numeral 142 follows dd. rn 'name' is r and n with the man with hand to mouth, n the genitive. ḥꜣd is the papyrus clump ḥꜣ with ꜣ and the hand d, with a shrine with a flared top (coded O21, approximate; perhaps the chest Q6) as classifier: a shrine or coffin (Budge: ḥaṭ, 'sarcophagus'); the word is not known otherwise. 'X is the name of Y' is a sentence without a verb or pw.

sentences.i: 'He is seen at once' is the name of the qeriu(?).
sentences.n: Budge's groups ḥer and à are joined here as ḥr-ꜥ 'at once', the face with its stroke and the arm with its stroke: the adverb, literally 'upon the arm' (Budge: 'upon [his] hand'). mꜣꜣ·tw·f is the eye with the sickle and ꜣ, as in line 134, then tw and ·f: the passive sḏm·tw·f, 'he is seen'. rn n as before. qriw is the hill q, r, a reed and w, with a low sign with crossed sticks at one end and a forked post at the other (coded U15, approximate) as classifier: a word not known otherwise, perhaps a shrine or enclosure, as Budge took it (qeràu); doubtful.

sentences.i: Another saying: it is the name of the block.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ky ḏd in red, the rest in black; the variant names the qeriu(?) of the line before. nmmt 'the block' is the upright knife nm (T34, approximate) with m and t, and a block with a knife laid across it (T28 with T30, approximate) and the house sign as classifiers: the place of slaughter, as in the Spell 125 declarations, where it is spelled n, m, m, t.

sentences.l: as-for · back(?) · bright · of-mouth · moving(?) · of-head · the-phallus · it-is · of · Osiris
sentences.i: As for 'back(?), bright of mouth, moving(?) of head', it is the phallus of Osiris.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes all of this in red. The gloss takes up line 133 without the name Rehu. In place of ḥꜣ·k 'behind you' it has sꜣ, the sign sꜣ (Aa18) with a stroke, the word for 'back' that is written in m-sꜣ 'behind': taken as a variant of the cry. It could also be sꜣ 'son', 'the son, bright of mouth', but 'son' is written with the pintail duck in the published parts. ḥḏ rꜣ as in line 133; psd and tp as there, tp with a stroke. ḥnn 'phallus' is the wick ḥ, a hoe (coded U6, approximate; the hoe ḥn), water n twice and the phallus (D53) as classifier. The noun and pw make the answer, 'it is the phallus', with n wsir 'of Osiris', the genitive after pw as it often stands. The being told to turn back is thus the god's own phallus.

sentences.l: another · saying · the-phallus · it-is · of · Ra
sentences.i: Another saying: it is the phallus of Ra.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ky ḏd in red, the rest in black. ḥnn pw is written as in the gloss before, with n rꜥ 'of Ra', the god with the sun on his head. Budge's numeral 144 stands before n.

sentences.l: as-for · have-loosened(?)-you · hair-your · tangle(?)-I · [n] · at · the-brow · is · Isis · it-is · at · hiding · in-it
sentences.i: As for 'you have loosened(?) your hair, and I tangle(?) it at the brow': it is Isis, who was hiding in it.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ir psdḫ·n·k šn·k tḫtḫ·i n r wpt in red; the answer is in black. The gloss quotes line 135 in another form: 'you' for 'he', the sḏm·n·f 'you have loosened(?)', and no 'his'. psdḫ·n·k is p, the bolt s, the hand d, the placenta ḫ and walking legs, with n and ·k: the verb of line 135, here with d, so that psḫ there may lack a sign, or psdḫ here have one too many. šn·k 'your hair' is the cord šn with n and the lock of hair. tḫtḫ·i as in line 135. Water n stands before r 'at': what it adds is not clear, and it is not translated. wpt 'the brow', the horns with t and a stroke, here without ·f; Budge prints the f in brackets in his transliteration only, and the papyrus has no sign for it. wnn is the hare wn (E34) with n and n: wnn with ḥr and the infinitive makes 'was (doing)', and pw is set inside it after the subject: 'it is Isis, who was hiding'. ḥr is the face with its stroke; štꜣ 'hide' is the pool, t and the kiln with ꜣ; im·s is the sign im with the folded cloth ·s: 'in it', the hair. Isis hides under her loosened hair, the gesture of mourning.

sentences.i: Then she smoothed(?) her hair there.
sentences.n: Budge's groups āḥā and en are joined here as ꜥḥꜥ·n 'then', the mast ꜥḥꜥ (P6) with the arm ꜥ and water n: the auxiliary that opens a narrative sentence, followed by a sḏm·n·f. sin·n·s is the folded cloth s, a reed, the fish in (coded K1) with n, and the low sign coded U15, then n and the bolt ·s: the sḏm·n·f of sin 'rub, smooth' (Budge: sàn, 'drawn'), 'she smoothed(?)'; the sense with hair is doubtful. šny·s 'her hair' is the cord šn with n, two strokes y and the lock of hair, and ·s. im 'there, therewith', a reed and the owl, refers back to the brow: she spread her hair over it.

sentences.l: as-for · Wadjet · lady · of-flame(?) · the-Eye · of-Ra · it-is
sentences.i: As for Wadjet, lady of flame(?), she is the Eye of Ra.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ir in red, the rest in black. wꜣḏyt is written as in line 140 but without the t; it is read the same. imw has an extra stroke before the flame. irt rꜥ 'the Eye of Ra' is the eye with t and a stroke and the god with the sun, the two nouns side by side, and pw makes the answer. The cobra on the brow of the sun is his Eye, the burning goddess who strikes his enemies. With these words Spell 17 ends on Ani's papyrus; Budge notes that other copies go on further.
